questions.prompt: A MOS capacitor has \(t_{ox} = 20\ \mathrm{nm}\). What is its capacitance per area in accumulation, in nF/cm²?
questions.explanation: In accumulation the holes act like a metal plate at the surface, so \(C = C_{ox} = \frac{3.45\times10^{-13}}{2\times10^{-6}} = 172.7\ \mathrm{nF/cm^2}\).

questions.prompt: In depletion, the MOS capacitance is modelled as:
options: \(C_{ox}\) in series with the depletion capacitance \(C_{dep} = \varepsilon_s/X_d\)
questions.explanation: A small change in gate charge is mirrored at the depletion edge, a depth \(X_d\) below the oxide, so the two dielectrics are in series: \(\frac{1}{C} = \frac{1}{C_{ox}} + \frac{X_d}{\varepsilon_s}\).

questions.prompt: An accumulation measurement gives \(C_{ox} = 3.45\ \mathrm{fF/\mu m^2}\). What is \(t_{ox}\), in nm?
questions.explanation:
\[3.45\ \mathrm{fF/\mu m^2} = 3.45\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{F/cm^2},\quad t_{ox} = \frac{3.45\times10^{-13}}{3.45\times10^{-7}} = 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{cm} = 10\ \mathrm{nm}\]
That is the standard way to measure oxide thickness electrically.

questions.prompt: At LOW frequency, why does the C–V curve rise back to \(C_{ox}\) in inversion?
options: Inversion electrons can form and vanish fast enough to follow the signal, so the charge changes right at the surface, just like in accumulation
questions.explanation: At high frequency, minority electrons (made by slow thermal generation) can't keep up. Then only \(X_{d,max}\) responds and \(C\) stays at \(C_{min}\).

questions.prompt: Within the depletion approximation, how does the capacitance of an n+/p MOS capacitor change as \(V_{GB}\) rises from \(V_{FB}\) to \(V_T\)?
options: It stays at \(C_{ox}\) until \(V_T\), then drops suddenly
It falls steadily from \(C_{ox}\) toward \(C_{min}\): \(X_d\) grows (as the square root of the silicon drop), so the series \(C_{dep} = \varepsilon_s/X_d\) shrinks
It rises, because more gate charge means more capacitance
It falls linearly with \(V_{GB}\) and reaches zero at \(V_T\)
questions.explanation:
\[\frac{1}{C} = \frac{1}{C_{ox}} + \frac{X_d}{\varepsilon_s},\quad X_d = \sqrt{\frac{2\varepsilon_s\psi_s}{qN_A}}\]
At \(V_{FB}\), \(X_d = 0\) and \(C = C_{ox}\). As the band bending \(\psi_s\) grows to \(-2\varphi_p\), \(X_d\) reaches \(X_{d,max}\) and C reaches \(C_{min}\). Gotcha: capacitance is \(dQ/dV\), not \(Q/V\), and it never goes to zero, because \(C_{ox}\) is still in series with a finite \(C_{dep}\).

questions.prompt: In accumulation, the \(t_{ox} = 20\ \mathrm{nm}\) capacitor is driven 2 V below \(V_{FB}\). What is the magnitude of the accumulated hole charge, in nC/cm²?
questions.explanation:
\[|Q| = C_{ox}|V_{GB}-V_{FB}| = 172.5\times2 = 345.3\ \mathrm{nC/cm^2}\]
Gotcha: use \(V_{GB}-V_{FB}\), not \(V_{GB}\). The charge is zero at flat band, not at 0 V.

questions.prompt: Gotcha: a C–V curve measured on a device with a THICKER oxide but the same doping would show:
options: A lower C_ox plateau and a shallower relative dip (C_min/C_ox closer to 1)
questions.explanation: \(C_{min}/C_{ox} = 1/(1 + C_{ox}X_d/\varepsilon_s)\). A smaller \(C_{ox}\) makes the oxide dominate the series combination, so the depletion layer matters less.

questions.prompt: Preview of MOSFET gate capacitance: a gate \(W = 2\ \mu\mathrm{m}\) by \(L = 2\ \mu\mathrm{m}\) with \(t_{ox} = 2\ \mathrm{nm}\) is in strong inversion. What is \(C_{ox}WL\), in fF?
questions.explanation:
\[C_{ox} = 17.25\ \mathrm{fF/\mu m^2},\quad C = 17.25\times4 = 69.1\ \mathrm{fF}\]
In saturation only about \(\frac{2}{3}\) of it appears from gate to source; that's covered in the device-capacitance skill.

questions.prompt: Preview of channel charge: with that 69 fF gate at \(V_{GB}-V_T = 0.5\ \mathrm{V}\), how many electrons are in the channel?
Preview of the operating regions: in an NMOS transistor biased at \(V_{GS} < V_T\), what charge does the gate capacitance mostly 'see'?
options: Depletion charge in the body (C_ox in series with C_dep), with almost no channel; the transistor is in cutoff
questions.explanation: Below threshold there's no inversion layer, so the gate couples to the body through the depletion layer. Above threshold the channel shields the body, and the gate sees about \(C_{ox}WL\).
